task.pr_title: Avoid taking a reference to a nullptr

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description: I don't understand this could end up taking a reference to nullptr, but if size() is 0 then s[0] is certainly illegal.  Are you saying string's internal char buffer is initialized to nullptr?  Because c_str() could be called on a newly initialized string I thought the internal buffer always had at least length 1 to include the '\0'.

evidence.thread_resolution:
baldersheim: Yes, it is &s[0] which is the problem. The vector's buffer is nullptr when nothing has been added, or space reserved.
hakonhall: What will c_str() do then if nothing has been added?  Return a pointer to a '\0' byte stored outside the buffer or will a buffer be allocated?
baldersheim: std::string has a buffer on the stack for up to 16 bytes which it uses for small strings before allocating any memory. The zero termination will be there if it is empty.
